title: What Does the Bible Say About Speaking in Tongues? 22 Verses
description: What the Bible says about speaking in tongues: Pentecost, Paul's rules in 1 Corinthians 14, the gift's purpose and whether it continues today.
keywords: what does the bible say about speaking in tongues
bible verses about speaking in tongues
summary: Tongues appears in 8 verses of the World English Bible and 34 of the King James Version, because the World English Bible often renders the Greek glossa as language. The gift first appears at Pentecost, when the disciples spoke so that visitors heard them in their own languages (Acts 2:1-11), and again in Cornelius's house (Acts 10:44-46) and at Ephesus (Acts 19:1-6). Paul lists tongues among the Spirit's gifts (1 Corinthians 12:7-11), ranks it below love and prophecy (1 Corinthians 13:1, 14:1-5), requires interpretation in church (14:27-28) and says not to forbid it (14:39). Churches disagree on whether the gift continues; Pentecostal and charismatic churches say yes, many others say it ended with the apostles.

faqs.q: What does the Bible say about speaking in tongues?
faqs.a: It describes tongues as a spiritual gift (1 Corinthians 12:10), first at Pentecost as known human languages (Acts 2:6-11) and in Corinth as speech that needs interpretation (1 Corinthians 14:2, 27). Paul says he speaks in tongues more than all of them, but prefers five words with understanding in church (1 Corinthians 14:18-19).

faqs.q: Is speaking in tongues for everyone?
faqs.a: Paul asks 'do all speak with tongues?' in 1 Corinthians 12:30 and the answer in the context is no. He also says he wishes everyone spoke in tongues but more that they prophesy (1 Corinthians 14:5).

faqs.q: What are the rules for tongues in church?
faqs.a: Two or three at most, one at a time, with an interpreter; if there is none, the speaker keeps silent (1 Corinthians 14:27-28). Paul ends with 'don't forbid speaking in tongues' and 'let all things be done decently and in order' (14:39-40).
Churches disagree. Continuationists point to Acts 2:39 and 1 Corinthians 14:39; cessationists point to 1 Corinthians 13:8, which says tongues will cease. The verses are below.
